units.en: He fought in Xinjiang, Hezhou, and Xining, won repeated distinction, rose to brigade general, and was granted the title Kense Batulu.
units.literal: He fought in turn in Xinjiang, Hezhou, and Xining, achieved merit repeatedly, was promoted in succession to brigade general, and was granted the title Kense Batulu.

units.zh: 既，還長沙，隸忠浩麾下。
units.en: He later returned to Changsha and served under Zhonghao.
units.literal: Afterward he returned to Changsha and served under Zhonghao.

units.zh: 宣統二年，補鎮筸鎮標中軍游擊。
units.en: In 1910 he was appointed central battalion commander of the Zhenqian garrison.
units.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he was appointed central battalion mobile corps commander of the Zhenqian garrison standard.

units.zh: 明年，武漢事起，忠浩電調援長沙。
units.en: The following year, when rebellion broke out at Wuhan, Zhonghao telegraphed for him to reinforce Changsha.
units.literal: The next year trouble broke out at Wuhan; Zhonghao telegraphed to summon him to aid Changsha.

units.zh: 次辰州，聞省城亂，乃扼辰龍關，誓死守。
units.en: At Chenzhou he heard the provincial capital had fallen into chaos and seized Chenlong Pass, swearing to hold it to the death.
units.literal: Stopping at Chenzhou, he heard the provincial capital was in disorder and therefore held Chenlong Pass, swearing to defend to the death.

units.zh: 筸兵故悍銳，為民軍所憚。
units.en: The Qian garrison was famously fierce, and the revolutionary army feared them.
units.literal: The Qian garrison troops were formerly fierce and sharp, and the revolutionary army feared them.

units.zh: 時總兵周瑞龍持兩端，其子瓚齎金至，將以餌筸兵，哨弁李鳳鳴潛告讓梨，得為備。
units.en: Brigade general Zhou Ruilong was wavering; his son Zan arrived with gold to bribe the Qian troops. Sentinel officer Li Fengming secretly warned Rangli, and he was able to prepare.
units.literal: At the time Brigade General Zhou Ruilong wavered between two sides; his son Zan brought gold, intending to buy off the Qian troops. Sentinel officer Li Fengming secretly informed Rangli, and he was able to prepare.

units.zh: 瑞龍稱疾，檄讓梨還，代以他將。
units.en: Ruilong claimed illness, ordered Rangli back, and replaced him with another officer.
units.literal: Ruilong claimed illness and ordered by dispatch that Rangli return, replacing him with another commander.

units.zh: 讓梨乃上書責以大義滅親，辭激昂，且傳檄捕瓚，瓚遁。
units.en: Rangli wrote a furious letter invoking the duty to put loyalty above family ties and issued a warrant for Zan's arrest; Zan fled.
units.literal: Rangli then submitted a letter rebuking him with the principle that righteousness overrides kinship, his words impassioned, and also issued a proclamation to arrest Zan; Zan fled.

units.zh: 已而瑞龍降，道府官委印綬去。
units.en: Before long Ruilong surrendered, and circuit and prefectural officials abandoned their posts.
units.literal: Before long Ruilong surrendered, and circuit and prefectural officials surrendered their seals and departed.

units.zh: 讓梨痛哭，犒遣軍士，獨棹小舟至清浪灘，踴身入水。
units.en: Rangli wept, rewarded and dismissed his soldiers, poled a small boat alone to Qinglang Beach, and threw himself into the water.
units.literal: Rangli wept bitterly, rewarded and dismissed the soldiers, alone poled a small boat to Qinglang Beach, and leapt into the water.

units.zh: 舟子泅出之，讓梨恚甚，曰：「奚活我為？」
units.en: The boatman pulled him out. Rangli was furious and said, "Why did you save me?"
units.literal: The boatman swam out and pulled him up. Rangli was deeply angered and said, "Why keep me alive?"

units.zh: 瓚出代其軍，遣人追縶讓梨及其子傳孔，鎖送長沙。
units.en: Zan took command of the troops and sent men to seize Rangli and his son Chuan Kong, who were shackled and sent to Changsha.
units.literal: Zan came forth to replace his army, sent men to pursue and seize Rangli and his son Chuan Kong, and had them locked and sent to Changsha.

units.zh: 迳常德，遇龍璋巡按西路，勸之不屈，遂斬之。
units.en: Passing through Changde he met Long Zhang, inspector of the western circuit, who urged him to submit; he refused and was beheaded.
units.literal: Passing through Changde he met Long Zhang on inspection tour of the western circuit, who urged him to yield; he would not bend, and was thereupon beheaded.

units.zh: 臨刑，肅衣冠北鄉拜，觀者萬餘人，皆泣下。
units.en: At the execution he dressed in his formal robes and bowed toward the north; more than ten thousand onlookers wept.
units.literal: Facing execution he arranged cap and robes and bowed toward the north; more than ten thousand onlookers all wept.

units.zh: 傳孔釋還。
units.en: Chuan Kong was released and sent home.
units.literal: Chuan Kong was released and sent back.

units.zh: 有陳萁者，讓梨從子壻也。
units.en: There was also Chen Qi, Rangli's nephew by marriage.
units.literal: There was one Chen Qi, Rangli's nephew by marriage.

units.zh: 當讓梨被縛時，萁即奪起擊縛者，僕一人，攢刃交下，傷其首，斷一足，並死之。
units.en: When Rangli was seized, Qi sprang up and attacked his captors. With a single servant he fought back until blades cut his head and severed a foot; both died.
units.literal: When Rangli was bound, Qi at once sprang up and struck the binders. With one servant, blades rained down together, wounding his head and severing one foot, and both died.

units.zh: 論曰：辛亥之變，各省新軍既先發難，防營不能獨支，而京外旗兵久無軍備，又多被殘困，死行陣者，自寥寥可數。
units.en: The historian comments: In the revolution of 1911 the provincial new armies struck first; defense garrisons could not hold alone. Banner troops outside the capital had long gone without proper arms and were often trapped and slaughtered, so those who died fighting were few.
units.literal: The commentator says: In the change of 1911 the new armies of the provinces had already risen first; defense camps could not hold alone, while banner troops outside the capital had long lacked military preparation and were mostly trapped and slaughtered—those who died in battle were naturally few and countable.

units.zh: 志鈞等權輕勢孤，艱難搘柱，思以一隅挽全局；
units.en: Men such as Zhi Jun held little power and stood alone, struggling to shore up the situation and hoping to save the dynasty from a single corner of the empire;
units.literal: Zhi Jun and others had light authority and stood alone, propping up the situation with difficulty, thinking to save the whole realm from one corner;

units.zh: 及事不可為，乃以死報，志節皎然，可敬亦可哀矣！
units.en: when nothing more could be done they repaid the dynasty with their lives. Their integrity shines bright—admirable and deeply moving.
units.literal: when affairs could not be saved they repaid with death. Their resolve and integrity shine clear—worthy of respect and also deeply pitiable!
